Extract geographic coordinates from pixel coordinates

Source: R/get_pts_coords.R
get_pts_coords.Rd

Transform target point pixel coordinates into longitude/latitude coordinates using a set of Ground Control Points (GCPs). This function performs direct point-wise coordinate transformation without warping a raster.

get_pts_coords(gcp, target_pts, transform_method = "auto", lambda = 1e-04)

Arguments

gcp

A data frame containing the Ground Control Points (GCPs). This dataframe can be produced with the draw_gcp_points function. This data frame should have the following columns:

  • id: An identifier for each GCP (numeric).

  • x: The x-coordinate of the GCP (in pixel space).

  • y: The y-coordinate of the GCP (in pixel space).

  • longitude: The longitude of the GCP (georeferenced).

  • latitude: The latitude of the GCP (georeferenced).

target_pts

A data frame containing the target points to transform. This dataframe must contain the following columns:

  • id: An identifier for each target point.

  • x or cx: The x-coordinate of the point (in pixel space).

  • y or cy: The y-coordinate of the point (in pixel space).

transform_method

A character string specifying the transformation method to be used for warping the image. Options are "poly_1" (first order polynomial), "poly_2" (second order polynomial), "poly_3" (third order polynomial), "tps" (thin plate spline), or "auto" (the default, automatically selecting a polynomial order based on the number of GCPs available).

lambda

Numeric smoothing parameter used for thin plate spline transformations (transform_method = "tps"). A value of 1e-4 produces near-exact interpolation through the GCPs, mimicking GDAL TPS behaviour whilst helping with algorithm convergence. Larger values introduce smoothing and may improve robustness when GCPs contain noise or digitizing errors.

Value

A data frame containing:

  • id: The original target point identifier.

  • Pixel coordinate columns from the original dataframe.

  • lon: Estimated longitude.

  • lat: Estimated latitude.

Details

Polynomial transformations are implemented using native linear models, while thin plate spline transformations are implemented using fields::Tps().

Note that, when using tps as a method, you might get warnings that the "Grid searches over lambda (nugget and sill variances) with minima at the endpoints:" This is often benign warning and indicates that the optimal smoothing parameter is at or near the boundary of the search space (matching the default lamba 1e-4, and thus approaching perfect interpolation).

Examples

pts_df <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata/europe_gcp_georef.RDS",
  package = "crstools"
))
target_df <- data.frame(pt_id = 1:2, x = c(477, 2014), y = c(554, 1311))
get_pts_coords(pts_df, target_df)
#>   pt_id    x    y longitude latitude
#> 1     1  477  554 -16.12353 36.84757
#> 2     2 2014 1311  14.67597 47.18133
